svg.text: 25 MB of weights must cross this boundary every single frame — the
floor on frame time no amount of extra multipliers can lower.
B · The path from one MAC operand to the DRAM chip
Every box that can hold a transaction, with its depth. This is where the board hang lives.
Why the accelerator stalls here
The cache serves one access at a time; the prefetcher answers from the
request presented at that instant. A pipelined host loses its responses.
Verified vs. stubbed
Cache and prefetch are exercised by student_gemm_ddrpath_tb.
blkmgr, CDC and PHY are still behavioural stand-ins — the open suspects.
C · One image, stage by stage
126 × 126 input · 9 × 9 grid of 14 × 14 patches · 82 tokens × 384 · 12 blocks · 6 heads × 64

g.text: PyTorch checkpoint → quantise weights to int8 with per-channel (multiplier, shift) → pack 299 tensors, plus the resized int16 image, into one blob.
export_dav2.py · numpy + torch · nothing on the board yet
Bitstream → FPGA. sw.elf (88 KB) → BRAM. Blob (24.87 MB) → DDR3 at 0x8000_0000, 1.2 min at 0.37 MB/s. Handshake flag written in BRAM.
81 patches of 14×14×3 → im2col → GEMM 81×588 @ 588×384 → 18.3 M MAC. Class token + position embedding added in float, requantised once.
image + weights read from the DDR3 blob · im2col and output in the arena · A-tile of 16 rows staged into accelerator BRAM
This is where the board currently stalls — the accelerator’s first DDR3 job.
3 · Twelve transformer blocks — 1.74 G MAC, the bulk of the frame
Four GEMMs per block go to the accelerator; everything else is scalar CPU work on a core with no FPU. Weights streamed from the DDR3 blob each time.
After blocks 3, 6, 9 and 12 the 81 patch tokens are LayerNormed and copied into a tap — 4 × 81 × 384, in the arena
Each tap projected 384 → 64 by 1×1 conv and reshaped to a 9×9 map · resized to four resolutions · fused coarse-to-fine through residual conv units
· output convolutions collapse 64 features to 1 channel · interpolate to 126 × 126 float.
taps, fusion maps and the depth image all live in the DDR3 arena; conv weights stream from the blob
ASCII depth art for immediate viewing, then the raw 126×126 float32 map hex-encoded between DAV2_RESULT_BEGIN / DAV2_RESULT_END.
printf → hostio OBUF ring in BRAM → OpenOCD polls it over JTAG → dav2_run_fpga.py decodes to fpga_depth.npy

svg.text: Per frame
2.412 G multiply-accumulates · 5.273 M requantised elements · 25 MB of weights crossing DDR3
The accelerator absorbs the MACs. Requantisation, LayerNorm, softmax, GELU, residuals, im2col and interpolation stay on a 50 MHz scalar core with no FPU,
so speeding up the matmul moves the bottleneck onto those and onto DDR3 bandwidth rather than removing it.
Status: stages 0–1 and the start of stage 2 have run on real hardware. Stages 2–5 have run only on the host, where the output matches PyTorch at
correlation 0.99984. No end-to-end depth map has yet been produced by the FPGA.
